newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm oil export taxes effective July.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm oil export taxes effective July.

text.p: Indonesia's new export taxes for crude palm oil and its products announced on Monday will be effective from July 1, a finance ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The new rates are effective from this month," he told Reuters.

"For this month, the amount of export taxes will be calculated using the free-on-board price of the item when the letter of credit (LC) opened by the importer is received by the Indonesian exporter," he said.
He said the government would not issue the export price for July, but added that the industry and trade ministry would issue the export price periodically.
Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad announced the new tax structure as part of the government's economic deregulation package that cut import tariffs on 1,600 items.
He said the tax on crude palm oil and its products averaged 10-12 percent between 1994 and 1996.

He said under the new structure, crude palm oil will be subject to an export tax of five percent, refined, bleached and deodorised (RBD) palm olein two percent, RBD palm oil four percent and crude olein four percent.
